title: Minimax Constant Collapse, Centered Diagonal Sandwiches, and Sharp Binary Lind-Singmaster Counting for Repeated Entries in Pascal's Triangle
abstract: We sharpen all three quantitative pillars of Leshem and Sayag (arXiv:2611.34736v1) on the density of repeated entries in Pascal's triangle. First, using only their existing inputs (Remond's effective bound and exact small-binomial tables), we collapse their uniform exponential constant from 2 to 113/100 = 1.13 for all x >= 3 and H >= 2 (a 43.5% cut), prove the exact minimax asymptotic limit (ln 5)^(1/4) ~ 1.1263375 with super-exponential blowup strictly below it, and halve the effective Bombieri-Pila exponent for A_2(x) from 1/6 to 1/12 (and A_3(x) from 1/12 to 1/15). Second, we prove a universal Stirling-centered falling-factorial sandwich yielding a zero-unknown-constant diagonal counting bracket that removes the systematic -3/4(K-1)(K+2) bias in A_1(x). Third, we derive exact Lucas identities for Singmaster's Fibonacci family, collapse the growth constant in Q(sqrt(5)) to (phi^4 / sqrt(5)) ln(phi), and prove the exact binary law #{F cap [1,x]} - floor((log log x - log c)/(4 log phi)) in {0, 1} for every x >= 3003 with 100% asymptotic density of exact floor equality. All algebraic cores are formally verified in Lean 4.35.0 (17 theorems, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) and 16 exact rational certificates.
